summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR459.9 crores and PAT 38% to INR78.2 crores, but FY26 revenue growth slowed to 12% amid weak seasonal demand.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR459.9 crores (up 24% YoY), EBITDA INR144.7 crores (up 26%, 31.5% margin) and PAT INR78.2 crores (up 38%, about 17% excluding a deferred tax adjustment). Full-year FY26 revenue was INR1,703 crores (up 12%), EBITDA INR544 crores (up 11%, 32% margin) and PAT INR282 crores (up 15.3%). Management attributed the weak full-year growth to the absence of seasonal volume uplift in Q2 and Q3 and weaker international patient flows, and said ~20% growth is targeted for FY27. Occupancy was 45.3% group-wide in Q4, with mature hospitals at about 52%.

segments.commentary: Revenue broadly flat at ~INR28.9 crore in FY26, hit by lower Bangladesh and African patient flows and Middle East air-connectivity disruption in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth target of around 20% while maintaining margins, per management.
Group blended occupancy expected at 56–58% (Q&A: 56–57% blended for the coming year); mature hospitals targeted at around 60%.
ARPP expected to grow about 5–6% annually; management prefers ARPP over ARPOB as a trend measure.

Maintenance capex about INR45 crore per year; growth capex of INR400–500 crore over the next two years for Gurugram, and INR300–350 crore for Coimbatore, Pune, Indore and other facilities (about INR65–70 lakh per bed).
Gurugram Sector 56 (125 beds) targeted for H2 FY28; Sector 44 (325 beds) for Q1 FY29; Coimbatore (130 beds) for H2 FY28; Pune (150 beds) under excavation.
Management plans to share a detailed new-geography growth plan within about three months.
capex_capacity: Added nearly 500 beds in FY26, the highest annual capacity addition in company history; about 900+ beds in execution, expected to complete in about 2.5 years.
Gurugram Sector 56 (125 beds) and Sector 44 super-specialty hub (325 beds) under construction; company owns the land in Gurugram.
Coimbatore regional hub (130 beds) in active construction; Pune regional greenfield hub (150 beds) has all statutory approvals and excavation has begun.
Seegehalli, Bangalore 80-bed greenfield spoke signed on lease, to be the seventh hospital in the city.

Indore: 100-bed build-to-suit hospital in permission stage, with a partner building base structure and semi-warm shell on a 20–30 year lease; Rainbow funds fit-outs and equipment; commissioning in about 2 years. Meanwhile Rainbow manages pediatric, obstetric and neonatal services (~25 ICU beds, effective 50–70 beds) in a 200-bed hospital owned by a doctor-entrepreneur; revenue accrues to Rainbow and it is not an O&M contract.
demand_pricing: Outpatient, inpatient discharge and delivery volumes grew 19%, 18% and 22% in Q4 respectively.
Management attributed the FY26 shortfall to seasonal demand: normalised seasonality would have lifted growth to about 18–20% versus 12% reported.
ARPOB grew about 8%, driven mainly by case mix and fertility; pricing contributes but was not quantified.
ALOS has held around 2.7 days for three years; management sees 2.7–2.8 days as appropriate.
Management says Rainbow is the largest pediatric provider in the country and approximately 20,000 deliveries a year make it likely the second- or third-largest maternity chain.
Chennai has performed about 10 liver transplants in the first year of the program; Bangalore has built about 60–70% of its pediatric specialty capability.
Company has engaged CRISIL for an industry study on pediatric healthcare; results pending.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 IP discharge growth was organic, and what did acquisitions contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired and newly added units contributed about 9–10% of IP growth; Guwahati and Warangal contributed about 7–8% of revenue growth, with volume mix said to be similar.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recent volume improvement is due to digital and marketing initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is implementing a new CRM and Hospital Information System; early signs are visible but not all of the volume uplift is attributed to them. More visible results are expected by end of Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can ALOS be reduced further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ALOS is clinically driven, at about 2.7 days for three years; changes in case mix could move it to 2.7–2.8 days.

qa_highlights.question: Indore arrangement: who funds the capex and what is the structure?
qa_highlights.answer: The partner builds base structure and leases a semi-warm shell for 20–30 years; Rainbow pays lease rent and invests in fit-outs and equipment at about INR65–70 lakh per bed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in mature-hospital occupancy and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Absence of seasonal uplift in Q2 and Q3 was the main reason; Q4 mature occupancy rose to about 52%. Management expects mature hospitals at about 60% in the coming year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Target assets with at least 50 operational beds that can scale to 100+; the search is pan-India, with no fixed geographic preference.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex is about INR45 crore a year; growth capex is INR400–500 crore for Gurugram over two years plus INR300–350 crore for other projects. The company has no debt and expects to fund the pipeline internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive impact of maternity consolidation among top players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rainbow is the leader in pediatrics and is likely second- or third-largest in maternity; it competes on larger hospitals (minimum 50 beds) rather than boutique players.

risks_watch: Occupancy: group occupancy was 45.3% in Q4 versus a 56–58% target; mature hospitals must recover from about 52% to about 60%.
Seasonality: management still depends on seasonal demand, and FY26 growth was 12% against an 18–20% normalised figure.
International patient inflows remain disrupted (Bangladesh, Africa, Middle East air connectivity); FY26 revenue was flat.
Execution: about 900 beds to complete in about 2.5 years, with Gurugram capex of INR400–500 crore and Gurugram timelines to FY29.
Quality consistency across new spoke hospitals, raised by a retail customer's comments on Vizag versus Hyderabad.
Q4 PAT growth of 38% is flattered by a deferred tax adjustment; underlying growth was about 17%.
Pharmacy revenue is not disclosed; costs are about 12–13% of revenue.
Cash balance was stated as ~INR700 crore and corrected to ~INR600 crore on the call; confirm in filings.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, clinical positioning and the balance sheet, but cautious on near-term occupancy and seasonality, which it attributed to the weak FY26 full-year numbers. Several answers on pharmacy revenue, market share and Indore economics were deliberately limited.
key_quotes: Rainbow delivering its highest ever quarterly revenue and achieving 20% year-on-year growth.
We remain the undisputed leader in this segment.
